messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert triggered: service=hosted-inference-prod severity=critical. Escalation policy=prod-24x7. Primary did not acknowledge. Attempting secondary -> secondary page suppressed by Quiet Hours policy (window=23:00-06:00). Manager escalation scheduled but suppressed due to suppression overlap. See PD incident: https://pagerduty.example/incidents/PDI-12345 :rotating_light:
oncall-alex: I didn't see a page come through. Phone was on but no vibration. Did PD actually fire the secondary?
incident-bot: PagerDuty log: first_trigger=1711112200, primary_sent=true, secondary_attempt=1711112205, secondary_status=suppressed_by_policy, manager_scheduled=1711112210, manager_status=suppressed_by_policy.
sre-maya: I'm on it. Seeing 5xx spike from inference-v2 cluster across us-west-2: ~12% error rate on token-service over the last 3m. Rolling window matches the PD alert. Pulling logs now.
oncall-alex: thanks maya. If secondary was suppressed, we need to make sure manager is paged manually if on-call can't ack. @manager-raj can you check availability?
manager-raj: I'm awake, pinged. I didn't get the automated escalation because our quiet-window overlaps with manual overrides. Noted. If primary and secondary both miss, we'll need manager on call even if suppressed.
sre-maya: repro steps: curl to /v1/generate returns 503 with "kv-cache overflow" and traceback in inference-runtime: "KVCacheEvictionError". Quick mitigation: scale inference replicas + clear KV cache on affected hosts.
infra-ops-tom: I'm prepping a scale-up now. Command I'll run: 
``` 
kubectl -n inference scale deploy/inference-runtime --replicas=10
for node in $(kubectl get pods -l app=inference-runtime -o name); do kubectl exec $node -- /usr/local/bin/kvcachectl flush || true; done
```
infra-ops-tom: starting scale (running now). ETA for new pods ~60s.
oncall-alex: I'm going to acknowledge the PD incident so paging stops and we can coordinate here. ACKing and marking incident owner.
incident-bot: ACK recorded by oncall-alex at 1711112228. PagerDuty note: acknowledgement will prevent further automated escalations.
sre-maya: after scale-up, 5xx dropped to ~1.2% within 45s. Rolling restart avoided so far. Continuing to watch for KV eviction noise.
manager-raj: good containment. @customer-success-cleo please prepare a short message for the few customers who saw degraded latency/errors — mark as "investigating" for now, no rollback required.
customer-success-cleo: drafting: "We experienced a short service degradation affecting inference requests in US-West. Our engineers identified an internal cache eviction issue and scaled capacity to restore service. We're monitoring and will follow up with a post-incident summary. No action needed on your side." Want to send to the 3 affected customer tenants now? :email:
manager-raj: yes, send now. Also create a follow-up task to add a PD rule exception so manager escalation is allowed if both primary and secondary are non-responsive even during quiet hours.
sre-maya: captured notes: root cause suspected: aggressive KV cache eviction under slightly elevated token sequences causing runtime crash path. Action items: 1) instrument eviction thresholds, 2) add KV eviction SLO alerts before PD critical, 3) PD rule exception for double-suppression.
oncall-alex: re: PD change, we should test with a staged incident to ensure manager gets page when both others are suppressed.
incident-bot: Incident closed (manual) by oncall-alex at 1711112260. Resolution: scale-up and KV cache flush reduced error rate. Follow-ups assigned to eng-runtime and oncall for PD policy update.
